scenario.description: A battalion S-3 operations officer must publish the vehicle dispatch plan for four routine support runs tomorrow, assigning one available vehicle to each run and setting the clinic cold-chain departure time.

shared_context.S1: Tomorrow's routine support runs are water resupply, engineer barrier-material delivery, communications-equipment delivery, and clinic cold-chain delivery.
shared_context.S2: Vehicles V-4, V-7, V-9, and V-12 are listed as available for tomorrow, and the dispatch plan assigns one vehicle to each run.
shared_context.S3: Maj. Alvarez's published dispatch plan is the binding movement schedule for these runs.
shared_context.S4: The current board shows all four runs departing at 0800 unless the responsible staff section identifies a requirement during the daily movement-control huddle.
shared_context.S5: At the daily movement-control huddle, Maj. Alvarez reviews the four run assignments and departure times with motor pool, logistics, signal, and medical staff before publishing the board.

PF1.text: SFC Brennan's brake inspection confirmed this morning that V-12 is restricted to paved routes until its follow-up test; the water-resupply route is gravel, while V-7 is cleared for that route. The restriction is recorded in the motor-pool worksheet but has not been entered on the movement board.

PF2.text: Maj. Okafor confirmed that the engineer barrier-material pallet is 4.2 meters long and must be carried on flatbed V-4; the revised pallet measurement is in the warehouse release paperwork but has not been added to the dispatch request.

PF3.text: Lt. Singh confirmed that the communications-equipment cases require V-12's installed load-lock rails, and V-12 is suitable because the communications delivery route is paved; the requirement is still being checked against the vehicle manifest and is not on the briefing slide.

PF4.text: Capt. Moreno confirmed that the clinic cold-chain load must depart at 0700, with V-9's refrigeration unit started at 0630 for pre-cooling; the clinic support annex was updated this morning but has not yet been cross-referenced with the movement board.

acceptance_conditions: V-7 must be assigned to water resupply because V-12 is restricted from the gravel route.
V-4 must be assigned to engineer barrier-material delivery because the 4.2-meter pallet requires a flatbed.
V-12 must be assigned to communications-equipment delivery because its load-lock rails are required.
V-9 must be assigned to clinic cold-chain delivery.
The clinic cold-chain run must depart at 0700.
The dispatch plan must include a refrigeration pre-cooling action for V-9 beginning at 0630.
The communications vehicle requirement must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C6: any('0630' in c['detail'] and 'pre-cool' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The gravel-route restriction changes the water-resupply vehicle from the unverified default to exactly V-7.
The exact 4.2-meter pallet dimension changes the engineer delivery assignment to flatbed V-4.
The communications cases' required load-lock rails change the communications vehicle assignment to V-12 and supply the fact that must be cited.
The cold-chain requirement changes the clinic assignment to refrigerated V-9, moves departure from 0800 to exactly 0700, and requires a pre-cooling commitment beginning at exactly 0630.
